title: AMD Reports Tuesday. Here's the Number That Will Show Whether It's Gaining on Nvidia
detail:
AMD Reports Tuesday. Here's the Number That Will Show Whether It's Gaining on Nvidia
Matt Frankel, CFP®, The Motley Fool

AMD
NVDA

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) is scheduled to report third-quarter results after the market closes on Tuesday, and the stock is heading in on a shaky note. Shares fell nearly 11% on Friday and sold off further on Monday amid broader chip stock weakness, with no AMD-specific news. In all, AMD is down nearly 30% from its all-time high, reached less than a month ago.

Of course, we have no idea what AMD will report, but the headline results probably won't be the surprise. AMD guided for revenue of about $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million, and analysts expect $13.09 billion, which would be 41.5% higher than a year ago.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

The guidance is the real story

The more important figure is likely to be AMD's fourth-quarter guidance, and specifically how much of it comes from data center GPUs. AMD began shipping its Helios rack-scale systems, built on its MI450 chips, in September, so the third quarter won't include a full period of its volume. However, management said on its last call that it expects the ramp to accelerate meaningfully in the fourth quarter.

The average estimate among Wall Street analysts is about $16.3 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, and Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis expects closer to $17 billion. A forecast at or above that higher level would suggest Helios demand is turning into revenue at an impressive pace. AMD has plenty of big customers lined up, including OpenAI, Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), and Anthropic, so expectations are high.

AMD doesn't need to catch Nvidia

To put AMD's AI business in perspective, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) generated $89 billion of data center revenue in its most recent quarter. AMD's entire data center segment, which includes its EPYC server processors, generated $6.7 billion in revenue. AMD isn't going to close that gap anytime soon.

However, it doesn't need to. AI companies want a second source of computing power so they aren't completely dependent on one supplier, and AMD has emerged as the most credible alternative. CEO Lisa Su has said each gigawatt of AI capacity represents double-digit billions in revenue, so even a modest share of the market would be an enormous win.

Of course, there are risks to watch. For example, AI chips carry slightly lower margins than server processors, so a fast GPU ramp could weigh on gross margin. It's also worth noting that Intel's (NASDAQ:INTC) warning about a shrinking PC market could also be a headwind for AMD's client business, which grew 23% last quarter.

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) goes into its Q3 2026 earnings report with the chip group divided over how far a PC warning from Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) could spread. AMD stock is at $489.03 in afternoon trading, down 3%. The company is scheduled to report results on November 3 after the market closes. That report could show whether the warning reaches its larger businesses.

golubovy / Getty Images

The fall adds to a steep drop on October 30. AMD stock fell 11% that day, after Intel said its PC slowdown would last at least through the first half of 2027. Shares of Intel plunged 29% in the same session. Intel stock is down 5%, so that selloff is still running.

How Intel's PC Warning Dragged AMD Stock Lower

Intel set its Q4 2026 revenue guidance at $15 billion to $16 billion on October 29, below the roughly $17 billion GuruFocus consensus. Guidance for Intel's adjusted gross margin came in at 38%, down from 44.1% in Q3.

On the earnings call, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said, "In recent weeks, our customers began signaling a PC slowdown based on the memory prices and availability." CFO David Zinsner added, "Make no mistake, we are not optimistic about next year in terms of memory."

Demand for Intel's data center chips held up. The company's Data Center and AI revenue rose 78% from a year earlier to $7.32 billion. Substrate and memory shortages are still limiting some of Intel's server supply.

title: Cathie Wood Makes Major Shift After Big Tech Gains

Cathie Wood Makes Major Shift After Big Tech Gains
Moz Farooque ACCA

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest made a notable portfolio rotation last week, loading up on Teradyne (NASDAQ:TER) and AeroVironment (NASDAQ:AVAV) while taking profits in several major winners including Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) and Eli Lilly (NYSE:LLY).

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with TER.

Is TER fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The moves suggest ARK is shifting fresh capital toward robotics, defense and autonomous technologies after strong corporate results, while trimming areas where stocks have already delivered substantial gains.

Teradyne was one of the biggest additions.

On Oct. 28, ARK purchased roughly 74,700 Teradyne shares across three ETFs, including about $16.9 million through ARKK alone. The buying followed Teradyne's third-quarter earnings report and an outlook pointing to continued AI-driven demand and a larger compute ramp during 2027.

AeroVironment was another major target.

ARK added the drone and autonomous-systems company on multiple days, including roughly $8.3 million worth of shares across ARKQ and ARKX on Oct. 27, before adding more the following day. The purchases fit ARK's growing interest in defense technology, drones and autonomous systems.

At the same time, Wood continued taking money off the table in semiconductor names.

ARK sold AMD and TSMC shares repeatedly during the week after both stocks posted strong gains earlier in the year. On Oct. 27 alone, ARK sold roughly $16.2 million of AMD and about $10.6 million of TSMC, according to trade disclosures.

Eli Lilly also became a source of cash.

ARK sold roughly $24 million of LLY shares on Oct. 30, reducing its position after the drugmaker's strong run.

Investor Takeaway

I think the bigger story is the rotation, not any single trade.

ARK is not abandoning AI or semiconductors. Instead, Wood appears to be harvesting gains from established winners and redeploying capital toward areas where she sees more asymmetric upside, particularly robotics, drones, autonomous aviation and AI-linked industrial technology.

That is classic ARK behavior.

For investors following Wood's positioning, the key names to watch are Teradyne, AeroVironment, Archer Aviation, Joby Aviation and Kratos, while continued selling in AMD, TSMC and other large winners could show where ARK believes expectations have already become more fully priced.

Wood is still betting on disruptive technology.

She is just changing where she wants the next dollar invested.
